briefing.headline: The simulation predicts the mandate would roughly triple departures over the next 12 months, from about 461 to about 1,390 of 5,000 employees (around 930 extra leavers, +215%). Treat the exact figure as a rough indicator of scale.
briefing.most_at_risk: Mid-level staff (+272%), caregivers (+266%) and long commuters (+229%) react worst. The most adamant voices combine caring for a child or parent with a commute of over an hour and say they are already job-hunting, while managers (+226%) object mainly to badge tracking as a sign of distrust.
risks: You would lose experienced people you can least afford to lose: mid-level staff and managers react more strongly than juniors, and several voices cite 6 to 11 years of tenure.
Badge tracking and VP-only exceptions are seen as distrust even by people who can manage the commute, so those who stay may disengage and keep job-hunting.

The burden falls unevenly on caregivers and, slightly, on women (+223% vs +210% for men), which creates fairness and reputational exposure. Rivals still offer flexibility, so these people have somewhere to go.
design_changes: Let each team choose its own in-office days based on when collaboration actually happens, instead of three fixed company-wide days. This keeps the 'come in when the team needs you' approach people already accept.
Drop individual badge reviews with managers, or limit them to anonymous building-level data. Tracking is the single most cited irritant, even among people who say they can live with the days.
Let direct managers approve exceptions against published criteria (caregiving, commutes over an hour), and phase the policy in more gradually than 90 days, for example starting at two days.
briefing.confidence: medium. Every group and every sampled voice moves the same way, so the direction is solid. But the size of the jump rests on just 48 modelled voices, and most say they are 'looking' rather than leaving, so actual exits could come in well below 1,390.

subgroup_checks.claim: Bigger rise for mid and senior managers
